To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SiPMs are promising candidates for the realization of a combined PET/MR insert.

(1) SiPMs are suitable for PET applications; (2) the energy resolution of the LYSO-SIPM detector is slightly better than that of the LSO-APDs; (3) no degradation of the performance was observed under MR conditions; (4) the non-linear behaviour of the SiPMs has to be taken into account for PET imaging; (5) optical crosstalk and dark counts are relevant issues in PET applications.
SiPMs are a promising technology for PET detector applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new PET detector concept for PET/MR imaging based on SiPMs and a sampling ADC data acquisition system, which has been shown to be feasible for PET/MR applications.
the design, characterization and optimization of a PET detector based on LYSO crystals coupled to SiPMs, for simultaneous PET-MR imaging.
the design of a novel PET detector module, which has been characterized for PET/MR applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LYSO-Single Photon Counting Detector Array (SPCD) is a promising candidate for PET/MR applications, but the non-linear behaviour of SiPMs should be considered in the design of future systems.
the SiPM-based detector modules are suitable candidates for PET insert applications in PET/MR systems, and that they are comparable with the currently used APD-based detector modules.
SiPMs can be used as a promising alternative to APDs as scintillator light sensors in PET.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SiPM arrays are promising for PET detector applications, especially in combination with MR.
the use of LYSO as scintillator in SiPM based PET detectors has a potential in the field of PET/MR.
SiPMs are a promising alternative to APDs as scintillator readout photodetectors for PET.

SiPM arrays are a promising technology for combined PET/MR applications, and that they are a good alternative to LSO-APDs. Proc. SPIE 9034, Medical Imaging 2014: Physics of Medical Imaging,
the SiPM detector concept is a promising candidate for combined PET/MR systems, as it provides a high sensitivity and a high time resolution with a compact design.
